title: No Verified Incident Can Defend Vietnam’s Dog Meat Trade
excerpt: No police record, court judgment, or health alert appears here to prove trade defenses. Rabies and theft still demand quarantine, transparency, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
When rabies symptoms appear, disease is virtually 100% fatal. That fact needs urgent action—but it does not prove that any specific dog-meat shipment caused any specific infection. No verified police seizure, court judgment, named location, or public-health incident appears in the available material. Honest advocacy must not fill that gap with invented victims or scenes.

Tradition cannot erase missing records

“Tradition” does not excuse stolen companions, illegal transport, uninspected slaughter, or failure to follow veterinary controls. Each claim needs records: police reports, court decisions, transport documents, quarantine findings, and traceable health alerts. Without those records, no responsible campaign can claim that every animal comes from a particular source—or that every trader commits a particular offense.

Farm claims need proof and quarantine

“Farm-raised” is not evidence by itself. Legitimate origin requires traceability, lawful transport, veterinary inspection, and quarantine compliance. Those safeguards protect Vietnamese families, workers, children, and animals. They also separate lawful activity from documented criminal conduct and from SDE’s proposed abolition policy.

Rabies demands immediate care

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. See WHO rabies guidance.

Vietnamese communities deserve records, enforcement, and protection from illicit operators. State rabies targets are not the same as SDE’s demand for complete abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
